messages:
emma: Heads up — privacy question. We have a feature that stores masked identifiers (one-way pseudonyms) in the de-id proxy for search/rate-limiting. DSAR came in asking for deletion. If we delete the mapping row we can’t prove we deleted the underlying PII because only the proxy had the mapping. Thoughts on KMS/RBAC and audit requirements for proving deletion to legal/compliance?

raj: Quick clarifying q: the mapping store is currently encrypted at rest with a single service-level key (redwood-deid-key), right? And access is via the proxy service account?

emma: Correct — single KMS key, proxy service account (svc-deid) reads/writes. Mapping TTL varies but can be persisted indefinitely for some customers due to rate-limit needs.

luis: Two high-level risks: 1) Single key + one service account = blast radius if compromised. 2) Deleting mapping rows doesn’t prove original PII was removed unless we have immutable audit trail showing who triggered delete and the pre-delete counts.

ola: For DSARs we need both evidence of deletion and a way to prevent rematerialization. If proxy was the only place mapping existed, we should: - ensure mapping creation events are logged (with hash, customer id, KMS key ID used) - when delete happens, emit a signed deletion receipt (timestamp, hashed id, operation id) and store that in audit log.

maria-legal: From legal POV we need: proof of action, identity of actor, timestamp, and retention exception flags if any. Signed receipts + immutable logs are fine. Also ask whether the mapping itself could be reconstructed from other telemetry — if so, deletion alone isn’t sufficient.

raj: Proposed technical changes: 1) Move to per-customer KMS keys (or per-tenant key derivation) so deletion can be scoped and key rotation/disablement effectively renders mappings unreadable. 2) Add RBAC so only a small set of human-run runbooks + svc-deid can perform deletes; require 2-person approval for permanent deletes.

sec-bot: deploybot: New IAM policy proposed: "deid-delete-approver" group. CI plan requires manual gating for key-disable actions.

luis: Implementation sketch: - store mapping rows as {pseudonym, ciphertext, kms_key_id, created_by, created_at, checksum} - on DSAR delete: mark row pending_delete, emit audit event, require approval api (/v1/deid/approve-delete) that records approver id, then call KMS to schedule key disable + zero-out ciphertext. After key disable and DB row overwrite with random bytes, emit deletion receipt.

emma: A couple of edge Qs: 1) For customers who need indefinite retention (contract), how do we handle retention exceptions vs subject rights? 2) Audit log retention length — legal wants receipts kept for 7 years for some contracts. Does that conflict with minimization?

maria-legal: Retention exceptions must be explicit in contract and surfaced in DSAR responses. For logs: you can retain deletion receipts as minimal metadata (hashed id, timestamp, actor) — that’s allowed for compliance evidence. Avoid storing PII in those receipts.

ola: On KMS approach: per-customer keys are ideal but costly. Alternative: derive per-customer data key via HKDF using a master KMS-wrapped key per-region; store only the wrapped per-customer data key in DB. To revoke you can delete the wrapped key or rotate master, then zero ciphertext. Works with RBAC for key unwrap.

raj: RBAC detail: add a short-lived role for "deid-delete-runbook" that requires MFA and has time-limited session length. All delete operations must be logged to immutable append-only storage (WORM). Use signed receipts where we sign with our signing key (not KMS data key) so receipts remain verifiable after key changes.

luis: Example deletion flow (pseudocode):
```
# request -> proxy validates DSAR -> writes pending_delete event to auditsrv
# approval -> ops CLI triggers: auditsrv.record(approver, op_id)
proxy.autoErase(op_id):
  db.update(mapping, set=ciphertext_random_bytes)
  kms.schedule_disable(kms_key_id)
  auditsrv.emit('deleted', op_id, hash(pseudonym), approver)
```

emma: How do we prove to the customer that their mapping was irrecoverable? If we overwrite the ciphertext and disable key, we can present the receipt and KMS disable timestamp, correct?

ola: Yes; present deletion receipt + KMS key disable/disable-version metadata + audit entries. For extra assurance, include checksum of the pre-delete ciphertext in receipt (not PII) so you can show there was material and it changed.

maria-legal: Also include certificate chain for the signing key used for receipts. Retain receipts per contract. If legal hold is triggered, keep a copy in e-discovery vault — document the exception.

raj: One more ops concern: rollbacks. If a deletion was accidental, we need a documented rollback policy. Our design should make permanent deletes require irreversible action (key destroy) and ephemeral deletes (mark deleted + TTL) for safer recovery.

emma: Thanks. Action items: 1) raj/luis/ola draft a design doc for per-tenant key wrap + approval flow. 2) luis to prototype audit-signed receipts (signed with signing-key). 3) ola to update DSAR playbook with retention-exception language. 4) sec-bot: create IAM ticket for deid-delete-approver group.

sec-bot: ticket created: IAM-8472. Assigned to raj, luis. ETA 3d. :white_check_mark:

luis: I’ll start a short RFC. Will include sample receipts and audit event schema.

emma: Perfect. If anything needs legal sign-off ping maria-legal. :thumbsup:
